title: Implement granular route crediting and proxy drain policy to stabilize toolcall streaming
author: Marissa Chen
description: Motivation: Intermittent stream stalls and payload replays were observed when tool/function-calling workloads hit route-level burst limits or when the proxy drained unevenly during overlap periods. This caused visible user-facing latency spikes and increased token costs for small-function-heavy sessions. Goal: introduce per-route credit accounting, conservative drain behavior in the streaming proxy, and small changes to the OpenAI-compat layer so fallback routes and structured function-call JSON remain stable under transient backpressure. Summary of changes: 1) Route crediting: add a lightweight in-memory credit bucket per route that decays on idle and refills on successful response commits. New config knobs: gateway.route_credit_window_ms (how long credits accumulate), gateway.route_initial_credits, gateway.route_min_drain_credits. This allows the router to prioritize low-cost/interactive routes over flushy bulk routes and avoid fast-fail churn. 2) Proxy drain policy: implement a two-phase drain where the proxy attempts a soft-drain (pause accepting new streaming fragments for a route when drain threshold reached) and then a hard-drain only after a grace period. New config: proxy.drain_threshold_percent, proxy.soft_drain_grace_ms, proxy.stream.buffer_target_bytes. The soft-drain queues fragments up to buffer_target_bytes and backpressures upstream rather than dropping or re-routing abruptly. 3) Tool/function calling stability: ensure fncall handshake is replay-safe across a soft-drain transition. The OpenAI compatibility layer now recognizes partial fncall frames and defers finalization until the route-credit check passes; a short-lived tombstone ensures duplicate tool-invocations are rejected during retry windows. 4) Payload sizing: introduce route-level max_route_payload_bytes (default 256k) and refine gateway-level max_payload_bytes to keep route shards balanced. 5) Observability and rollback: emit new metrics (route_credit_used, proxy_soft_drain_count, fncall_tombstone_hits) and add dashboard panels and alerts. Rollout plan: staged rollout by Canary ring -> 50% traffic -> global. Feature gated behind gateway.feature.route_crediting and proxy.feature.soft_drain. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve current behavior; soft-drain disabled unless enabled in config. Testing: unit tests for credit accounting, integration e2e with streaming harness, and a new perf canary that runs toolcall-heavy episodes for 2h. Checklist: - [x] Credit accounting algorithm implemented and unit-tested - [x] Proxy drain soft/hard phases implemented - [x] OpenAI-compat changes for fncall handshake added - [x] Metrics + dashboards wired - [x] Integration tests and perf canary updated - [x] Feature flags added and documented

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Major - the credit decay math looks like it could underflow on long idle routes; please add a floor and a test for 7d idle windows.
Marissa Chen: Addressed - added a min_credit floor and idle test for 7d; updated comments with invariants. PTAL.
Priya Nair: Nit - please extract the magic numbers into config defaults and document rationale. Also verify that the default max_route_payload_bytes won't break large file->embedding paths.

release_notes: Gateway: add per-route credit accounting to reduce churn under bursty toolcall workloads
Proxy: soft-drain policy to gracefully backpressure streaming fragments instead of abrupt re-routes
OpenAI-compat: fncall handshake made replay-safe across soft-drain transitions
Observability: new metrics route_credit_used and proxy_soft_drain_count
Config: new flags gateway.feature.route_crediting and proxy.feature.soft_drain (off by default)
